newsitem.title: USA: GFOA panel urges mark-up rules for govt securities.
newsitem.headline: GFOA panel urges mark-up rules for govt securities.

text.p: A GFOA panel voted on Saturday to urge the National Association of Securities Dealers to get moving and write standards for what constitutes appropriate mark-ups in the sale of government securities.

The Government Finance Officers Association's cash management committee warned that recent charges of "yield burning" in the municipal bond market have highlighted the need for mark-up rules for government securities.
The GFOA panel added that any NASD mark-up rule should require dealers to disclose mark-ups in advance of sale to customers, if the investors request the information.

The GFOA panel approved the standard during a meeting at the association's annual conference here. GFOA's executive board is set to vote on the draft policy on June 2 and the group's general membership votes June 3.

The panel approved the policy despite objections from some members. "I don't know what kind of a message we are going to be sending by doing this," said one finance officer. "This is the latest attempt by us to legislate common sense," he said.

But Betsy Dotson, GFOA assistant director and counsel to the cash management committee, pointed out that finance officers "worked hard" in the early 1990s to get Congress to include language authorizing NASD to write mark-up rules in the Government Securities Act Amendments of 1993.

"If we don't step out ... we abdicate responsibility" on this issue, she said. Dotson conceded that at least one provision of the policy -- disclosure of mark-ups upon request -- is viewed by some as "radical." She said the language could be revised.
But the panel voted to leave the concept in.

The draft policy says, "GFOA views the adoption by market regulators of mark-up guidelines and the requirement to disclose mark-ups, if requested, as essential to assure just and equitable trading." It adds that "use of a competitive selection process" also is essential.

Currently, NASD has a five percent mark-up guideline for equities, but no specific standard for government securities. The group says that excessive mark-ups in government securities have always been viewed as a violation of the group's rules of fair practice.

NASD proposed a mark-up rule for government securities in August 1994, but has taken no further action. The Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board has not adopted specific mark-up guidelines, although it bars sales in excess of a "fair and reasonable amount, taking into consideration all relevant factors..."
The cash management panel's policy does not recommend a particular percentage mark-up standard.
